-

global smuggled brands in the market – introduction of new variants and own trademarks with 
international appeal 
- 
Sharp increase in seizures of smuggled cigarette consignments by enforcement agencies across the 
country, signalling growing exploitation by unscrupulous players and anti-social elements of the 
widening tax arbitrage opportunity in the Indian market. 
 
• 
Agri Business Segment delivers Revenue growth of 12% YoY led by Value Added Products & Leaf Tobacco 
exports 
 
- 
Overall Agri Business remains impacted by West Asia conflict led disruptions and delayed call offs by 
customers  
▪ New market development initiatives stepped up to diversify into other geographies 
- 
Strong growth in Value-added Agri products (VAAP) driven by Spices and Fruits & Vegetables 
- 
Lower domestic demand due to unprecedented tax increase on Cigarettes continues to affect overall 
leaf tobacco business  
▪ Leaf Tobacco exports perform well leveraging strong customer relationships, globally recognised 
sustainability credentials and crop development & processing expertise.  
 
• 
Strong Recovery momentum in Paper Segment; Segment Revenue up 36% YoY (LTL 10%) & Segment PBIT 
up 48% YoY (LTL 52%); Segment PBIT margin expands 320 bps 
 
- 
Improving demand scenario; Pricing actions mitigate severe inflation in input costs  
- 
Robust performance in anchor grades of value-added products, sustainable portfolio and exports  
- 
Wood prices remain elevated due to lower-than-expected harvest and demand from competing 
industries; moderation in prices expected going forward 
- 
Minimum Import Price on Virgin Multi-layered Paperboard extended till 31st March 2027; Industry 
continues to engage with policymakers for sustained safeguard measures in respect of low-priced 
imports of paperboards and coated/uncoated paper. 
 
• 
Fresh Food Business continued its robust growth trajectory  
 
- 
GMV grew 53% YoY; ARR crosses Rs. 320 cr. 
- 
7 new kitchens opened during the quarter; footprint expanded to 80+ cloud kitchens 
- 
‘Prasuma Chilli Chow’ launched to expand the portfolio with a street-style Chinese offering. 
 
 
 
The operating environment continued to be characterised by heightened uncertainty amidst renewed 
geopolitical tensions and trade disruptions. Crude oil and crude-linked input prices remained elevated, while 
supply chain disruptions and higher freight costs persisted. Global inflationary pressures intensified, driven by 
higher energy and food prices, alongside elevated sovereign bond yields and tighter financial conditions. In India, 
headline inflation moved up, driven by a broad-based increase across food, fuel and core components.

domestic demand across rural and urban markets. However, deficient and uneven monsoons and lower reservoir 
levels, alongside strengthening El Niño conditions, pose risks to agricultural output and the inflation trajectory. 
Geopolitical developments, climatic conditions, inflationary headwinds and consumer sentiment would remain 
key monitorables. 
 
The macroeconomic fundamentals of the Indian economy remain resilient, supported by proactive and agile 
policy actions by the Government of India. Sustained public capex, improving trends in private capex, strong 
credit growth, healthy bank and corporate balance sheets, and measures to curb foreign exchange volatility and 
strengthen investment activity augur well for sustained growth of the Indian economy.

- 
Reinforcing its commitment to making nutritious everyday foods more accessible, the brand 
augmented its portfolio with the launch of ‘Aashirvaad Sathu Mavu’ in select markets 
- 
Value-Added variants and Staples adjacencies have grown three-fold over the last 5 years, with 
salience in the portfolio doubling over this period. 
 
• 
‘Aashirvaad’ Salt sustained its strong volume-led growth momentum, supported by its distinctive 
positioning of ‘Iodine Assured salt for a Smarter India’.  
 
• 
‘Sunrise’ Spices delivered strong growth and strengthened its market standing in the core market of 
West Bengal while gaining ground in the neighboring markets of the Northeast, Bihar and Jharkhand.

Norohinkopaat Masala’, in line with the brand’s promise of serving the unique tastes and preferences 
of consumers across regions.

in volumes and higher realisations (mix enrichment & pricing). The ‘Sunfeast Dark Fantasy’ range of 
indulgent cookies further fortified its leadership in the premium segment. Recent launches, including 
‘Sunfeast Mom’s Magic Shines’ and ‘Sunfeast Baked Creations’, are scaling up well. The portfolio was
